selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main warning is given in this conclusion about loving worldly life too much?
questions.answer: Being fooled by this life can make a person forget the hereafter and live in heedlessness.

questions.question: Which part of a person is being addressed in this passage?
questions.answer: The lower self, or nafs, is being addressed.

questions.question: How is the nafs described at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as careless, attached to this life, and forgetful of the next life.

questions.question: What animal is used in the comparison?
questions.answer: An ostrich.

questions.question: Why does the ostrich put its head in the sand in the comparison?
questions.answer: It is trying to avoid facing the hunter.

questions.question: Why does that action not actually save the ostrich?
questions.answer: Its body is still exposed, so the danger has not gone away.

questions.question: What is the point of saying the ostrich cannot see the hunter?
questions.answer: It shows that closing your eyes to danger does not remove the danger.

questions.question: In the comparison, what remains uncovered even after the ostrich hides its head?
questions.answer: Its large body remains uncovered.

questions.question: What is the passage asking the nafs to do instead of hiding?
questions.answer: It is asking the nafs to reflect honestly on its condition.

questions.question: What Qur’anic message is placed at the start of the conclusion about worldly things?
questions.answer: It teaches that the attractions of this world are deceptive and cannot be trusted as lasting success.

questions.question: What does the passage say is wrong with the nafs’s view of life?
questions.answer: It sees worldly life as pleasing and enough by itself.

questions.question: What important reality has the nafs neglected?
questions.answer: It has neglected the hereafter.

questions.question: What does the nafs focus on instead?
questions.answer: It focuses only on this worldly life.

questions.question: What creature is used to make this lesson easier to understand?
questions.answer: An ostrich is used.

questions.question: What danger appears in the example with the ostrich?
questions.answer: A hunter appears.

questions.question: How does the ostrich respond to the hunter?
questions.answer: It hides its head instead of escaping properly.

questions.question: What lesson does this teach about denial?
questions.answer: Denial may hide the truth from a person’s attention, but it does not change the truth.

questions.question: Which one has the heedless nafs forgotten?
questions.answer: It has forgotten the hereafter.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the biggest spiritual problem of the nafs?
questions.answer: Its biggest problem is heedlessness.

questions.question: How does heedlessness affect the nafs’s priorities?
questions.answer: It makes worldly life seem sweetest and pushes the hereafter out of mind.

questions.question: What is the nafs mainly chasing in the passage?
questions.answer: It is chasing worldly life alone.

questions.question: What comparison is used to expose the nafs’s mistake?
questions.answer: The nafs is compared to an ostrich.

questions.question: What truth is the heedless nafs refusing to face?
questions.answer: It is refusing to face the reality of the hereafter and the emptiness of living only for this world.

questions.question: What two realities are placed in contrast in this passage?
questions.answer: The passing world is contrasted with the hereafter.
